item.title: Witchweed menaces maize farms across Africa: New study maps the damage
item.description: Over $1 billion a year. That is what a small parasitic weed plant costs maize farmers across sub-Saharan Africa every year, without ever being caught in the act. Striga, known as witchweed, latches onto maize roots underground and siphons off water and nutrients long before it breaks the surface. By the time a farmer sees the damage, the blame falls on drought or exhausted soil. For 30 years nobody could put a reliable figure on the bill, and without one, the response stayed scattered. Fuente: Phys.org.

Pero más tarde se descubrió que Plutón era demasiado pequeño para explicar esas anomalías, así que el planeta X, que ya sería el décimo del Sistema Solar, se puso de nuevo sobre la mesa. item.title: Electron microscopy reveals the headquarters of poxviruses
item.description: Mpox remains a smoldering threat, with recent clusters in Brazil, Thailand and Austria and ongoing hot spots across multiple African countries. Other poxviruses also endanger human or animal health. A new study by the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) uncovers the inner workings of the poxvirus core: how its gene-copying machines sit parked in dormant pairs, ready to print viral instructions and release them into the host cell through dedicated export portals embedded in the core shell. Fuente: Phys.org.
